chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazantī asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has a wife and remains silent and does not speak. He said:

"Is he mute?" I said: "Yes, and we know from him hatred toward his wife and aversion to her. Is it permissible that his guardian divorce on his behalf?" He said: "No, but he should write and have witnesses over that."

I said: "May Allah rectify you, he neither writes nor hears; how does he divorce her?" He said: "By that through which he is recognized from his actions, like what you mentioned of his aversion and hatred toward her."

key_terms.أَخْرَسُ: a mute person who cannot speak
key_terms.أَفْعَالِهِ: his actions by which intention is recognized
key_terms.يَكْتُبُ: he writes to express his intent
key_terms.يُشْهِدُ: he takes witnesses over the act

ai.seo_question: How can a mute man issue divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding the divorce of a mute man. It states that his guardian may not divorce on his behalf; rather, his own intention must be conveyed through writing and witnesses, or through clear actions that indicate his intent when writing is not possible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4806 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (as) about a man who has a wife but remains silent and does not speak.

Imam (as) asked: "Is he mute?"
He replied: "Yes, and we know from his behavior that he dislikes and detests his wife. Is it permissible for his guardian to divorce her on his behalf?"
Imam (as) said: "No, but he should write it down and have witnesses for it."

He said: "May Allah (swt) correct you, but he neither writes nor hears. How can he divorce her?" Imam (as) replied: "Through actions that clearly indicate his intention, such as what you mentioned of his dislike and hatred for her."
